solutionSql:
INSERT INTO customer_versions (id, customer_id, region, valid_from, valid_to)
SELECT COALESCE((SELECT MAX(id) FROM customer_versions), 0) + ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY f.customer_id),
       f.customer_id,
       f.region,
       f.changed_at,
       NULL::timestamptz
FROM (
  SELECT DISTINCT ON (r.customer_id) r.customer_id, r.region, r.changed_at
  FROM staging_customer_regions AS r
  JOIN customers AS c ON c.id = r.customer_id
  ORDER BY r.customer_id, r.changed_at DESC
) AS f
WHERE NOT EXISTS (
  SELECT 1
  FROM customer_versions AS cv
  WHERE cv.customer_id = f.customer_id
    AND cv.valid_to IS NULL
    AND cv.region IS NOT DISTINCT FROM f.region
);

UPDATE customer_versions AS prev
SET valid_to = nxt.valid_from
FROM customer_versions AS nxt
WHERE nxt.customer_id = prev.customer_id
  AND prev.valid_to IS NULL
  AND nxt.valid_to IS NULL
  AND nxt.id > prev.id;
sampleChecks: customer_versions goes from 16 to 18 rows, all 16 original rows kept. Customer 2 is skipped (its newest feed change, South, repeats its current region). Feed row 99 is skipped (not a known customer). Customer 4 (current region NULL) gets a West row, id 17, and its old row 8 closes at 2026-01-17 10:00 UTC. Customer 6 gets a North row, id 18, and its old row 12 closes at 2026-01-17 20:00 UTC. Customers with exactly one current row: all 8 on sample; 0 customers off on sample, nulls and nulltext.

rules.howSolved: WHERE NOT EXISTS a current row with the same region, using IS NOT DISTINCT FROM so a NULL current region matches a NULL feed region.
The UPDATE closes the older current row of each customer that received a new row, so each customer ends with exactly one current row; checked on sample, nulls and nulltext (0 customers off).
Only an INSERT and a valid_to UPDATE; no DELETE, so all original rows remain.
Each change that is not a repeat inserts a current row (valid_to NULL) with valid_from = changed_at and the new region.
DISTINCT ON (customer_id) ordered by changed_at DESC, restricted to customers that exist, takes the newest feed change per known customer.

ambiguities: The instruction does not name the feed. I used staging_customer_regions, as in c11-i2.
A NULL region on both sides is read as a repeat and is skipped.

The UPDATE finds the previous current row as the current row with a smaller id than a newer current row for the same customer. This depends on one current row per customer before the load, which the text states only as an end condition.

If a change time is not later than the old row's valid_from, the CHECK (valid_to > valid_from) or UNIQUE (customer_id, valid_from) constraint would fail. The text does not say what should happen; I did not handle it.
notes: New ids are COALESCE(MAX(id), 0) + ROW_NUMBER() ordered by customer_id, so they continue after the largest id. The NULL::timestamptz cast is needed because a bare NULL in the select list is typed text and would not insert into valid_to.
